name: io.github.2016judea/marginalia-corpus
title: Marginalia Corpus
description: What famous readers marked in their books: Melville, Harvey, Dee, Whitman, Derrida, Beckett

tools.name: reader_marks
tools.description: The marks one reader left in the books of one author, or in one title, from the Marginalia Corpus. Answers questions like 'what did Melville mark in Shakespeare?', 'what did Derrida write in the margins of Rousseau?', 'show me Melville's notes in Beale's Natural History of the Sperm Whale', 'how much did Gabriel Harvey annotate his Livy?'. Returns counts by kind of evidence, kept separate: own_words (the reader's own words in the margin), bare_marks (a score, underline, bracket or checkmark), attested_copies (the reader held or borrowed the copy, no surviving mark), each also counted in the reader's certain own hand. Lists the volumes (edition, library, shelfmark, link) and, where the source's terms permit quotation, the passages: marked_passage is the book author's printed words under the mark, reader_wrote is the reader's own words, each with a citation line. For Archaeology of Reading (Harvey, Dee, Winthrop), the Walt Whitman Archive and the Beckett Digital Library the text is withheld under their terms and only counts, pages and metadata are returned. Reader, author and title names are matched loosely; a name that matches nothing comes back with the closest names.

author.description: Optional: the author whose books were marked, e.g. 'Shakespeare', 'Homer', 'Rousseau'.

title.description: Optional: words from the book's title, e.g. 'Sperm Whale', 'Paradise Lost', 'Macbeth'.

kind.description: Optional: which passages to list. own_words = the reader wrote something; bare_marks = a mark with no words. Default all.

own_hand_only.description: Optional: true lists only passages the source attributes to the reader's own hand with certainty (Melville's Channing volumes, for instance, are mostly his wife's or uncertain).

contains.description: Optional: only passages whose text contains these words, e.g. 'whale'.

tools.name: who_read_author
tools.description: Every reader in the Marginalia Corpus with documented evidence of reading one author, in separate groups that are never merged: marked (left own words or bare marks in a copy of the author), held_or_borrowed (owned or borrowed a copy, no surviving mark, including Shakespeare and Company lending-card borrows in Paris 1919-1941, dated to the day), named_in_their_writing (named the author in their own published work or a marginal note: Nietzsche's prose, Derrida's De la grammatologie, Harvey's and Dee's notes), and named_as_a_person_in_a_note. Answers questions like 'who read Homer?', 'which writers borrowed Joyce from Sylvia Beach?', 'who marked Shakespeare?', 'did anyone annotate Montaigne?'. Each reader comes with counts per kind of evidence, life dates and source. include_lending_library=false leaves out the 253 lending-library members and keeps the annotators.

include_lending_library.description: Optional: false leaves out Shakespeare and Company lending-card members. Default true.

limit.description: Most readers to list per group (default 25).

tools.name: reader_profile
tools.description: One reader's whole record in the Marginalia Corpus: volumes held, volumes with marks, counts by kind of evidence (own words, bare marks, attested copies, and how many are certainly in the reader's own hand), a per-source breakdown with whether its text is quotable, the most-marked authors, the authors the reader names in their own writing, the people named in their notes, and a date span (life, edition years of the copies held, and reading dates where the source attests them). Answers questions like 'what did Melville read?', 'tell me about John Dee's library', 'who did Nietzsche name most?', 'what did Hemingway borrow from Shakespeare and Company?'. One person with two records (Samuel Beckett: his own library and a Paris lending card) is returned as one reader.

tools.name: authors_read_by_many
tools.description: Authors that two or more readers in the Marginalia Corpus have evidence of reading, most readers first, each with the readers and their evidence kept per kind (marks, attested copies, references). Answers questions like 'which authors did the most readers mark?', 'what did Melville and Beckett both read?', 'which authors did three or more annotators physically mark?', 'who are the most borrowed authors at Shakespeare and Company?'. evidence picks the kind that counts: any, marked (own words or bare marks only), held_or_borrowed, or named. readers keeps only authors that every named reader reached.

evidence.description: Which kind of evidence counts a reader in. Default any.

readers.description: Optional: only authors reached by every one of these readers, e.g. ['Melville', 'Beckett'].

exclude_lending_library.description: Optional: true leaves out Shakespeare and Company lending-card members. Default false.

tools.name: search_marginalia
tools.description: Full-text search over the marginalia text that the sources permit quoting: Melville's Marginalia Online (Melville's notes and the lines he marked), Derrida's Margins (his annotations and the passages he marked, plus his quotations of other authors in De la grammatologie), Annotated Books Online (notes by Dee, Luther, Erasmus, Scaliger and others, with translations), and Nietzsche naming other authors in his published works. Answers questions like 'did Melville mark "nothing can come of nothing"?', 'which marginal notes mention the whale?', 'where does Derrida quote Saussure on writing?', 'what does Nietzsche say about Wagner?'. Accent- and case-insensitive; phrase match first, then all words. Archaeology of Reading, Walt Whitman Archive and Beckett Digital Library text is not in the searchable set, under their terms.

query.description: Words or a phrase to find, e.g. 'whale', 'nothing can come of nothing', 'écriture'.

reader.description: Optional: only this reader's marks, e.g. 'Melville'.

author.description: Optional: only marks in this author's books, or references to this author.

where.description: reader_words = what the reader wrote (notes, translations, their own published prose); marked_passages = the printed lines they marked. Default all.

tools.name: about_the_corpus
tools.description: The Marginalia Corpus at a glance: totals (555 readers, 9,303 volumes, 216,552 marks, 11,774 references), the three kinds of evidence, each of the eight source archives with its counts, whether its text is quotable, its terms and the citation it asks for, every annotating reader with their counts, and the most frequent Shakespeare and Company lending-library borrowers. Answers questions like 'what's in the marginalia corpus?', 'which readers are covered?', 'where does this data come from?', 'how should I cite it?'.

tools.name: did_reader_read_author
tools.description:
A yes or no, with the evidence, for whether one reader in the Marginalia Corpus read one author: marks they left in a copy (own words and bare marks), copies they held or borrowed with no surviving mark (including Shakespeare and Company lending-card borrows), references to the author in their own writing, and mentions of the author as a person in their notes. Each kind is reported on its own and never added together. A no means the surviving record holds no evidence, not that the reading never happened.

Example questions:
- "Did Melville read Shakespeare?"
- "Did Beckett read Proust?"
- "Did Nietzsche ever mention Schopenhauer?"

tools.name: what_reader_wrote_in_margins
tools.description:
Only the notes one reader wrote in their own words in the margins of their books (not bare underlines or scores), from the Marginalia Corpus, optionally narrowed to one author, one title or a word. Each note comes with the printed passage it sits beside, the page, whether the source attributes the hand to the reader with certainty, and its cite line. Text a source withholds under its terms is counted, not quoted.

Example questions:
- "What did Melville write in the margins of his Milton?"
- "What notes did John Dee leave in his books?"
- "Derrida's handwritten notes on Rousseau"

author.description: Optional: the author whose books carry the notes, e.g. 'Milton'.

title.description: Optional: words from the book's title.

contains.description: Optional: only notes or passages containing these words.

own_hand_only.description: Optional: true keeps only notes the source attributes to the reader's own hand with certainty.

tools.name: what_reader_said_about
tools.description:
Search one reader's own words in the Marginalia Corpus for a subject: their marginal notes, translations they wrote in, and (for Nietzsche and Derrida) their own published prose. The book author's printed lines are left out, so every hit is the reader speaking. Each hit carries the book, the page and its cite line.

Example questions:
- "What did Melville say about God in his margins?"
- "What did Nietzsche write about Wagner?"
- "What did Luther write about Christ in his books?"

subject.description: Words or a phrase to find in what they wrote, e.g. 'God', 'Wagner', 'whale'.

tools.name: what_readers_both_read
tools.description:
The authors that every one of two to six named readers has evidence of reading in the Marginalia Corpus, most readers first, with each reader's evidence kept by kind (marks, attested copies or borrows, references in their writing). Narrow to one kind of evidence with evidence.

Example questions:
- "What did Melville and Beckett both read?"
- "Which authors did John Dee and Gabriel Harvey both read?"
- "Authors Gertrude Stein and Hemingway both borrowed"

evidence.description: Which kind of evidence counts. Default any.

tools.name: shakespeare_and_company_borrowing
tools.description:
Sylvia Beach's Shakespeare and Company lending cards (Paris, 1919-1941): who borrowed an author, with the most-borrowed titles and each member's dates; or, for one member, every author and title on their card. A borrow is attested contact with a copy, dated on the card, not proof of reading.

Example questions:
- "What did Hemingway borrow from Shakespeare and Company?"
- "Who borrowed Joyce from Sylvia Beach's library?"
- "What did Gertrude Stein borrow from Sylvia Beach?"

author.description: The author borrowed, e.g. 'Joyce', 'D. H. Lawrence'. With reader, narrows that member's card to this author.

reader.description: A lending-library member, e.g. 'Hemingway', 'Gertrude Stein', 'Walter Benjamin'.

limit.description: How many borrowers or authors to list (default 25).
